fig1_blackbody_uv_catastrophe.svg:
Black-body spectral energy density $u(
u,T)$ from planck_u_nu at $T=4000,5800,7000$ K: each curve peaks and rolls over, the peak sliding to higher $
u$ (shorter $\lambda_{max}$, Wien displacement) and the area growing as $T^4$ (Stefan-Boltzmann). The classical Rayleigh-Jeans law (dashed) instead diverges as $
u^2$ — the ultraviolet catastrophe that Planck's energy quantum $E=h
u$ removed.
fig2_hydrogen_spectrum.svg: The hydrogen emission spectrum as a stick plot, every line placed by rydberg_wavelength$(n_1,n_2)$. The three lowest series — Lyman ($n_1{=}1$, ultraviolet), Balmer ($n_1{=}2$, straddling the visible band) and Paschen ($n_1{=}3$, infrared) — each converge to a series limit (dotted) as $n_2\to\infty$. Bohr's quantized levels $E_n\propto-1/n^2$ reproduce the observed lines, e.g. the red Balmer H$\alpha$ at 656 nm.
